data_section_full_text:
Our main sample is comprised of all firms in the Compustat database during 2006

through 2008, and the number of observations in each test is determined by the data requirements

for each dependent measure, as discussed previously. Our measure of religiosity comes from a

database of over 610,000 interviews conducted nationwide by the Gallup organization (see also

Omer et al. 2010). Gallup randomly selects 1,000 adults daily for these telephone interviews,

and participants are asked three questions relating to religion. As discussed previously, we

aggregate county-level responses to the three Gallup questions into a single measure of

religiosity at the MSA level.22 We identify 236 unique MSAs that are the location of company

headquarters for at least one company in our sample between 2006 and 2008.  Data for our tests

of financial reporting irregularities are obtained from several sources including Compustat, Audit

Analytics, Audit Integrity, CRSP, and I/B/E/S.


21 Inferences remain the same when we control for earnings management using the absolute value of discretionary
accruals (Cohen et al. 2008).
